analyst_view.overall: Early view: City won their first seven games and then lost three in a row, the last a 3-1 defeat at Forest where Enzo Maresca said they did not match the intensity. Marc Guehi and Josko Gvardiol came off with knocks and City host Napoli in the Champions League on 24 November. Leeds under Daniel Farke are a tight side (10 scored, 8 conceded) who just ended a winless run against Spurs.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.8 goals. I lean slightly lower: Leeds' games have averaged under two goals, and they defend in a compact back three with James Trafford in good form. City have conceded from transitions lately, but Leeds rarely commit enough men forward to exploit that.

corners.text: The site has 9.5 corners. I lean higher: City will have most of the ball against a deep Leeds block, and the more City are held up, the more they work it wide to Jeremy Doku and others. Corners for City should pile up.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.7 cards. I agree: Leeds can be physical, with Jayden Bogle lucky to escape a red against Spurs, but Leeds will spend most of the game defending in shape and City, with the ball, have less need to foul. Around four is fair.

shots.text: The site has 24.8 shots, only 15.6 for City. I lean higher: after three defeats City will come out hard at home, and a Leeds side that sits deep tends to give up many low-quality shots. City in the high teens looks realistic.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.0 shots on target. I agree: more City shots should come, but Leeds block a lot and Haaland may be crowded out. Antoine Semenyo is targeting a return from a knee injury around this time, which would add another threat if he makes it.
